title: Lisbon, October 2023
summary: Four-night solo trip based near Principe Real. The trip worked well because the city was walkable, evenings were mild, and there were enough cafes, viewpoints and restaurants to keep the plan flexible.
whatWorked: Principe Real and Chiado were good bases for walking without feeling too isolated at night.
Late afternoons at viewpoints were a highlight.
Food markets and small restaurants made rainy spells easy to work around.
Public transport was useful, but the best parts of the trip were short walks between neighbourhoods.
whatDidNotWork: Some steep routes became tiring when trying to fit in too much.
The busiest parts of Baixa and the tram routes felt less enjoyable at peak times.
A day with persistent rain needed a slower indoor plan.
weatherNotes: Comfortable when daytime temperatures were around 20-23C and evenings were cool but pleasant. Light rain was acceptable because there were indoor food and culture options nearby.
futureRecommendation: Lisbon is a strong fit in October if the forecast is mild and rain risk is not dominant. Prefer staying central, planning one main neighbourhood per day and keeping a flexible indoor backup.
